name: Ibiza
title: Holidays in Ibiza
intro: A UNESCO-listed old town, quiet pine-fringed coves and famous sunsets, well beyond the big clubs. Here's what Ibiza is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The walls and houses of Dalt Vila, Ibiza's old town, rising above the sea under a blue sky
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June and September are the best months for beaches and coves without the peak crowds. July and August are hot, busy and pricey. The big clubs open from late spring to early October. Winter is mild and peaceful, good for walking and the old town, but many hotels and beach places close.

things.name: Dalt Vila
things.blurb: Walk up through the Renaissance walls of Ibiza Town's old quarter to the cathedral and views over the harbour.

things.name: Cala d'Hort and Es Vedrà
things.blurb: A beach facing the mysterious rock island of Es Vedrà. Come for sunset.

things.name: Formentera
things.blurb: A short ferry to an island of white sand and very clear, shallow water.

things.name: Las Dalias hippy market
things.blurb: A craft and fashion market in Sant Carles, held on Saturdays, with night markets in summer.

things.name: Santa Gertrudis
things.blurb: A pretty inland village with a white church, cafés and art shops.

things.name: Cala Comte
things.blurb: Turquoise water and rocks on the west coast. A favourite spot for sunset drinks.

faqs.question: Is Ibiza only for clubbing?
faqs.answer: No. San Antonio and Playa d'en Bossa are the party areas, but the north and east are quiet, with coves, villages and rural hotels.

faqs.question: Is Ibiza expensive?
faqs.answer: It's one of Spain's priciest islands in summer. Coming in May, June or September and staying outside the party areas helps.

faqs.question: Do you need a car in Ibiza?
faqs.answer: Buses run between the main towns, but a car is the best way to reach the coves and villages.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Ibiza?
faqs.answer: Four or five days covers the old town, a few beaches and a day on Formentera. A week is more relaxed.
